name: CareBridger
notes: Relevant coordination substitute; pricing is CAD and subject to early-access caveat.
positioning: Shared care circles with tasks, reminders, calendar, notes, contacts, and care reports.
pricing: FACT: published plans list CA$0/month, CA$9.99/month Family Plus, and CA$18.99/month Care Circle Pro; the page says no payment is currently collected during early access.
strengths: Combines shared tasks, calendar, history, and role-based access.
target_customer: Families coordinating care for one or more care recipients.
weaknesses: Early-access status; paid-plan adoption and retention are unknown.

evidence_type: FACT: official App Store and terms; limited public complaint evidence
name: Medisafe
negative_feedback: Public Reddit discussion reports frustration with premium pricing and manually entering medication data; not a representative review sample.
notes: Relevant for medication subtask only; no claim that it solves broader care coordination.
positioning: Medication-management mobile app with paid Premium options.
pricing: FACT: Apple App Store lists monthly Premium options including US$4.99 and annual options including US$39.99; prices may vary by country/platform.
strengths: Focused medication workflow with published app-store pricing.
weaknesses: Narrower than full family-care coordination; user-reported public discussion cites subscription cost and manual medication entry as friction.

category: care communication and support coordination platform
name: CaringBridge
notes: Relevant substitute for family-update and support-coordination portions of the job.
positioning: Private health updates plus support-community activation and care coordination.
pricing: FACT: official support site describes a no-cost, private page; no subscription price published.
strengths: Free, private, ad-free communication and support coordination.
target_customer: Care recipients, caregivers, family, and support communities.
weaknesses: Designed primarily for updates/support rather than comprehensive medical, financial, or task administration.

category: care calendar and volunteer coordination platform
name: Lotsa Helping Hands
notes: Relevant family-workload alternative; satisfaction data beyond testimonials was not established.
positioning: Central care calendar for meals, rides, tasks, and updates.
pricing: FACT: official site calls the service free; no paid consumer plan was found.
strengths: Directly addresses volunteer task and ride coordination.
Free and simple for a support community.
target_customer: Caregivers coordinating friends, family, and volunteers.
weaknesses: Official positioning is support logistics, not financial administration or care-plan management.

business_model: Employer/health-plan benefit and private paid subscription.
category: care concierge and employee caregiving benefit
evidence_type: FACT: official plan and FAQ pages
name: Wellthy
notes: Relevant premium substitute across coordination, administration, and care-capacity work.
positioning: Human care coordinators handle logistical, administrative, in-home, insurance, and facility tasks.
pricing: FACT: official plan page lists private access at US$475/month for one month or US$400/month for three months; employer/health-plan members may use it at no cost.
strengths: Human-assisted service handles exceptions and administrative complexity.
Published private-pay plan and employer benefit channel.
target_customer: Employees with employer/health-plan access and private-pay families needing a care coordinator.
weaknesses: High private monthly price relative to consumer coordination apps; access is often employer-dependent.

business_model: Local private-pay service; some insurance/benefit offsets may apply.
name: Visiting Angels
notes: Relevant paid alternative for care-capacity work, not a software competitor. Do not generalize local rates nationally.
positioning: Local agency-delivered in-home care, including errands, rides, medication reminders, and respite.
pricing: FACT: published local pages vary. Coral Springs lists US$28-36/hour by care type; Chaska describes US$40-48/hour agency care and US$425-500+/day live-in care. These are local examples, not national pricing.
strengths: Human service can absorb physical tasks, transportation, and respite.
Local published price examples show existing service spend.
target_customer: Older adults and families purchasing local in-home companion, personal, or dementia care.
weaknesses: Pricing, minimums, and service availability vary by location and care level; local pages require a quote for many arrangements.
